# firecrawl download (invoked as `firecrawl x download`)

> **Experimental.** `download` is available under the `firecrawl x` command group.

**Prerequisite:** `download` requires authentication (no keyless free tier); without credentials the CLI prompts an interactive login.

Maps the site origin first to discover pages, then scrapes each one into nested directories under `.firecrawl/`. Use `--include-paths` to scope a non-root URL to one section. Automated runs always pass `-y` — without it the command opens an interactive wizard that blocks on a prompt.

## Quick start

```bash
# With screenshots
firecrawl x download https://docs.example.com --screenshot --limit 20 -y

# Multiple formats (each saved as its own file per page)
firecrawl x download https://docs.example.com --format markdown,links --screenshot --limit 20 -y
# Creates per page: index.md + links.txt + screenshot.png

# Filter to specific sections
firecrawl x download https://docs.example.com --include-paths "/features,/sdks" -y

# Skip translations
firecrawl x download https://docs.example.com --exclude-paths "/zh,/ja,/fr,/es,/pt-BR" -y
```

Run `firecrawl x download --help` for the full option list, including which scrape options download supports.

**Done when:** the command exits successfully and the expected files exist under `.firecrawl/`.

## See also

- [firecrawl-map](../firecrawl-map/SKILL.md) — just discover URLs without downloading
- [firecrawl-scrape](../firecrawl-scrape/SKILL.md) — scrape individual pages
- [firecrawl-crawl](../firecrawl-crawl/SKILL.md) — bulk extract as JSON (not local files)
- [firecrawl-build-scrape](https://github.com/firecrawl/skills/tree/main/skills/build/firecrawl-build-scrape) — building bulk extraction into an app instead of running it here

content.text:
I scraped 415 method pages from docs.slack.dev, which is 335 unique methods once the lowercase duplicate URLs are removed. I read the "Rate Limits" line on each page. Tiers come straight from those pages.

## Tier 1 (1+ per minute): 17 methods
- `admin.apps.uninstall`
- `admin.conversations.restrictAccess.removeGroup`
- `admin.teams.create`
- `admin.usergroups.addChannels`
- `admin.usergroups.create`
- `admin.usergroups.fetch`
- `admin.usergroups.update`
- `admin.users.unsupportedVersions.export`
- `apps.icon.set`
- `apps.manifest.create`
- `apps.manifest.delete`
- `apps.manifest.update`
- `apps.uninstall`
- `conversations.listConnectInvites`
- `rtm.connect`
- `rtm.start` (deprecated, see below)
- `team.externalTeams.disconnect`

## "Special" tier ("Special rate limits apply"): 18 methods
- `admin.analytics.messages.metadata`
- `agents.conversations.archive`
- `agents.conversations.create`
- `agents.conversations.listViews`
- `agents.conversations.removeView`
- `agents.conversations.setCommands`
- `agents.conversations.setProperties`
- `agents.conversations.setView`
- `apps.event.authorizations.list`
- `assistant.search.context`
- `assistant.threads.setStatus`
- `auth.test`
- `blocks.validate`
- `chat.getPermalink`
- `chat.postMessage`
- `oauth.v2.access`
- `oauth.v2.user.access`
- `tooling.tokens.rotate`

The method pages only say "Special rate limits apply" and don't give numbers. `chat.postMessage` is the one most likely to be hitting you. Its limits are described in the general rate-limits guide, which I didn't scrape.

## `conversations.*` methods: 28
| Tier | Methods |
|---|---|
| Tier 1 (1+/min) | `listConnectInvites` |
| Tier 2 (20+/min) | `acceptSharedInvite`, `archive`, `canvases.create`, `close`, `create`, `externalInvitePermissions.set`, `inviteShared`, `list`, `rename`, `requestSharedInvite.approve`, `requestSharedInvite.deny`, `requestSharedInvite.list`, `setPurpose`, `setTopic`, `unarchive` |
| Tier 3 (50+/min) | `approveSharedInvite`, `declineSharedInvite`, `history`, `info`, `invite`, `join`, `kick`, `leave`, `mark`, `open`, `replies` |
| Tier 4 (100+/min) | `members` |

`conversations.list` is Tier 2, the tightest of the commonly used ones. If you page through it often, caching its results is the easiest saving. `conversations.history` and `conversations.replies` are Tier 3.

## Deprecated on their own page
- **`rtm.start`**: the description begins "Deprecated: … Use rtm.connect instead," and the page has a deprecation banner linking to the changelog. It is also Tier 1.
- **`users.setActive`**: the description says "Deprecated and non-functional." It is Tier 2.
- **`files.upload`**: the page says the method "has been deprecated" and was to be sunset on November 12, 2025. It is Tier 2. Its description line doesn't say deprecated, so I found it from the body text.

Every page lists `deprecated_endpoint` and `method_deprecated` among its generic error codes. I ignored those.

## Limits of this check
- The list comes from a site map of 415 URLs. If the map missed any pages, those methods aren't covered.
- My deprecation search matched banner and description wording. A deprecation notice phrased some other way could have slipped through.
- The raw data is in `/tmp/fceval-c1-t2-w7hrvgbc/work/`. `rates.txt` has every method with its tier, and `pages/` holds the scraped pages.
